objectives: Choose a separation method from the properties of the substances.
Describe filtration, evaporation, crystallisation, distillation and chromatography.
Calculate Rf values and use melting/boiling points as tests of purity.

blocks.title: Elements, compounds, mixtures
blocks.md: An **element** has only one kind of atom. A **compound** has two or more elements **chemically combined** in a fixed ratio and has different properties from its elements (sodium + chlorine → sodium chloride). A **mixture** has substances **not chemically combined**; each keeps its own properties and they can be separated physically. A **pure** substance has a sharp, fixed melting and boiling point.

blocks.title: Choosing a method
blocks.md:
- **Filtration**: insoluble solid from liquid (sand from water).
- **Evaporation / crystallisation**: dissolved solid from solution (salt from sea water; crystallise slowly for large crystals).
- **Simple distillation**: solvent from solution (pure water from salt water).
- **Fractional distillation**: liquids with different boiling points (ethanol from water; crude oil).
- **Separating funnel**: immiscible liquids (oil and water).
- **Chromatography**: coloured substances (inks, dyes).
- **Magnet**: iron from a non-magnetic solid.

blocks.tex: R_f = \frac{\text{distance moved by the spot}}{\text{distance moved by the solvent}}
blocks.caption: Rf is always between 0 and 1 and has no unit

blocks.title: Distillation set-up
blocks.md: In **simple distillation** the solution is boiled, the vapour passes through a **condenser** (cooling water enters at the **bottom** and leaves at the top) and the pure liquid is collected. The thermometer bulb is at the **side-arm opening** to read the vapour temperature. Chromatography paper must be marked with a **pencil** line (ink would run) and the start line must be **above** the solvent level.

blocks.caption: Simple distillation: the solution is boiled, the vapour is cooled in the condenser and pure water is collected.
blocks.alt: A round flask on the left connected by a tube through a condenser to a collecting beaker on the right.

blocks.title: Example 1 — salt and sand
blocks.statement: Describe how to obtain dry sand and solid salt from a mixture of the two.
steps: Add water and stir: salt dissolves, sand does not. Filter: sand stays on the filter paper (wash and dry it).
Heat the filtrate (salt solution) in an evaporating dish until crystals start to form, then leave to crystallise and dry the crystals.

blocks.title: Example 2 — chromatography
blocks.statement: In a chromatogram a dye spot has moved 3.6 cm while the solvent front has moved 9.0 cm. Calculate its Rf value. Another dye has Rf = 0.8: where is it?
steps: A spot with Rf = 0.8 moves 0.8 × 9.0 = 7.2 cm, so it lies higher up the paper than the first spot.
blocks.answer: Rf = 0.40; the other spot is at 7.2 cm

exercises.source: Original exercise written for CastBridge, in the style of the curriculum
exercises.prompt: Explain how you would separate a mixture of ethanol (b.p. 78 °C) and water (b.p. 100 °C).
exercises.model: Use fractional distillation: heat the mixture; ethanol, with the lower boiling point, boils off first and rises up the fractionating column, condenses in the condenser and is collected at about 78 °C. Water, with the higher boiling point, stays in the flask.
exercises.rubric: 1 mark: fractional distillation; 1 mark: ethanol boils first (lower b.p.); 1 mark: collect at about 78 °C.
